terms.gloss: the seashore as a place of pleasure, a beach
evidence: Cic. Verr. 2.5.25: in actā jacēbat (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Greek ἀκτή, with a short a: the shore as a place of resort (Lewis & Short). Not to be confused with ācta, deeds, records.

phrases.english: After breakfast we’ll go down to the beach.

phrases.latin: Eāmus in lītus! Situlam et pālam cape.
phrases.english: Let’s go to the beach! Get your bucket and spade.

phrases.latin: quī in lītore ambulāns scalmum repperisset
phrases.english: who, walking on the beach, had found a thole-pin

sources: Lewis & Short: litus
Lewis & Short: acta
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 277.
